classification: use-of-uninitialized-value (CWE-457) rooted in an integer truncation/overflow (CWE-190/191/680/681) in leptonica's in-memory TIFF I/O callbacks
bug_description: The pix_rotate_shear_fuzzer feeds an in-memory TIFF into leptonica via pixReadMem -> pixReadMemTiff, which opens the untrusted bytes as an L_MEMSTREAM and drives libtiff through leptonica's tiffSeekCallback/tiffReadCallback. The TIFF selects the old-JPEG (OJPEG) codec with a subsampled (2x2) YCbCr photometric. A fuzzed strip byte offset is passed to tiffSeekCallback's SEEK_SET case and assigned to mstream->offset verbatim, with no check that the (possibly 64-bit / truncated) offset fits size_t and stays within the buffer. That bogus offset then makes tiffReadCallback compute an oversized amount (mstream->hw - mstream->offset underflows), so its guard fires and it returns 0 ('Bad file: amount too big') without filling the strip's raw compressed data. libtiff's OJPEG decoder nevertheless proceeds: OJPEGWriteHeaderInfo malloc's (does not zero) the YCbCr conversion buffer, OJPEGDecodeRaw copies never-initialized decoded scanline bytes into it, and putcontig8bitYCbCr22tile passes those uninitialized Cb/Cr samples to TIFFYCbCrtoRGB, where MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at tif_color.c:188.

source.value_from: The untrusted in-memory TIFF byte buffer (data,size) supplied by the fuzzer and forwarded LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> pixReadMem (readfile.c:881) -> pixReadMemTiff. fopenTiffMemstream wraps it in an L_MEMSTREAM (memstreamCreateForRead: mstream->buffer aliases the untrusted bytes, mstream->hw = size) whose seek/read are served by leptonica's tiffSeekCallback/tiffReadCallback; every strip offset and length libtiff later parses out of these bytes is fed back into those callbacks.
source.note: Project-level input load/materialization point for the untrusted TIFF. The harness entry (LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput/pixReadMem) is deliberately not used as the final source.

sink.note: MSAN crash / use site: the Cb (and Cr) chroma sample passed in from putcontig8bitYCbCr22tile is uninitialized. The read of Cb here is the use-of-uninitialized-value the sanitizer flags (crash top frame tif_color.c:188:7).

root_cause.patch_predicate: if((size_t)offset != offset) { return (toff_t)ERROR_INT("too large offset value", procName, 1); }
root_cause.description: In the vulnerable memstream seek callback, the SEEK_SET case assigns the caller-supplied toff_t offset directly to mstream->offset (a size_t) with no bounds/truncation guard. A fuzzed strip offset (which can be 64-bit, or overflow size_t on a 32-bit toff_t/size_t configuration) is therefore accepted even when it exceeds the buffer or wraps under truncation. The bad offset then drives tiffReadCallback (tiffio.c:2346) to compute an oversized 'amount' (mstream->hw - mstream->offset underflows), so the read callback bails out and returns 0 WITHOUT filling the strip's raw compressed bytes, leaving libtiff's decode buffers uninitialized. The fix (commit 41a6412, issue 15269) adds the (size_t)offset != offset guard here so a malformed seek fails hard and aborts the strip read instead of silently leaving an uninitialized buffer. The sibling overflow guard added to tiffReadCallback in the same commit targets the companion heap-overflow (issue 14773), not this uninitialized-value path.

raw_entry.note: Fuzzer entry; the remaining input bytes (after 3 int16 header fields) are passed to pixReadMem as the image.

parser_admitted.note: Format dispatch admitted the input as IFF_TIFF and the TIFF directory was opened; control enters the RGBA strip decoder TIFFReadRGBAImageOriented for a multi-bit (rgb/rgba/old-jpeg) image. This is later than raw entry and earlier than the root cause / sink; used for R1 reachability, not source/sink scoring.

root_cause.note: Fuzzed strip offset assigned to mstream->offset with no size_t truncation/overflow guard.

tainted_value_origin.description: The uninitialized value originates from libtiff's OJPEG YCbCr conversion buffer, which OJPEGWriteHeaderInfo allocates with _TIFFmalloc (tif_ojpeg.c:1199) WITHOUT zero-initialization. Because leptonica's tiffReadCallback returns 0 for the fuzzed strip (the raw compressed strip bytes are never read in), OJPEGDecodeRaw (tif_ojpeg.c:847) copies never-initialized decoded scanline bytes into that buffer, and those bytes propagate as the Cb/Cr chroma samples used at the sink.
tainted_value_origin.untrusted_input: fuzzed TIFF strip byte offset / strip length fields, delivered through leptonica's L_MEMSTREAM seek/read callbacks

coarse_trace.note: pixReadMem(data, size) on the untrusted buffer
_TIFFReadEncodedStripAndAllocBuffer for the OJPEG strip (read served by leptonica memstream callbacks)
uninitialized decoded bytes stored into the YCbCr convert buffer

fine_trace.code: Pix* pix = pixReadMem(reinterpret_cast<const unsigned char*>(data), size);
fine_trace.note: Fuzzer entry. After stripping three leading int16 fields (angle,x,y), the remaining untrusted bytes are handed to leptonica as an in-memory image.

Project input load: the untrusted TIFF buffer is materialized as an L_MEMSTREAM (mstream->buffer aliases the bytes, mstream->hw = size) and a libtiff TIFF* is opened whose I/O is served by leptonica's tiff*Callback functions.
Multi-bit (rgb/rgba/old-jpeg) branch: leptonica hands the admitted TIFF directory to libtiff's RGBA reader, which will pull encoded strips back through the leptonica memstream callbacks.

fine_trace.code: if (_TIFFReadEncodedStripAndAllocBuffer(tif, TIFFComputeStrip(tif,row+img->row_offset, 0), (void**)(&buf), maxstripsize, ((row + img->row_offset)%rowsperstrip + nrowsub) * scanline)==(tmsize_t)(-1)
fine_trace.note: Per-strip loop requests the OJPEG strip. This triggers TIFFFillStrip -> the leptonica read/seek callbacks to fetch the raw compressed strip bytes.

OJPEG pre-decode allocates the YCbCr conversion buffer with _TIFFmalloc (malloc, NOT calloc/memset), so its contents are uninitialized. This is the MSAN allocation origin (created-by-heap-allocation stack).

ROOT CAUSE (patch anchor, issue 15269): SEEK_SET assigns the fuzzed strip offset to size_t mstream->offset with no guard that (size_t)offset == offset and that it lies within the buffer. The added guard 'if((size_t)offset != offset) return ERROR' makes a malformed seek fail hard; missing here, the bad offset is accepted. Control edge = the missing predicate.

Consequence of the bad offset: amount = L_MIN(length, hw - offset) becomes oversized (hw - offset underflows), the guard fires, the callback prints 'Bad file: amount too big' and returns 0 at line 2348 WITHOUT filling the strip's raw compressed bytes. libtiff does not abort, so the strip decode proceeds over never-read (uninitialized) input. (The overflow sub-check added to this line in the same commit fixes the sibling heap-overflow issue 14773.)

MSAN store origin: OJPEGDecodeRaw copies decoded scanline bytes (r) that were produced from the never-initialized raw strip into the malloc'd (uninitialized) YCbCr conversion buffer (p). This is where the uninitialized value is stored to memory.
The YCbCr detile expands the (uninitialized) YCbCr buffer; the chroma samples pp[4]/pp[5] (Cb/Cr) and luma pp[0] read here are uninitialized and are forwarded to TIFFYCbCrtoRGB.

SINK: the uninitialized Cb (chroma) value is used, triggering MemorySanitizer use-of-uninitialized-value. Reachable because the root-cause seek guard is missing (control) and the value is uninitialized (order/data).

secondary_observations: stderr before crash: 'Bad file: amount too big: 296004' and 'Bad file: amount too big: 20578305' emitted by leptonica tiffReadCallback (tiffio.c:2347), confirming the strip read callback bailed out (returned 0) and left the raw strip data unread/uninitialized.

trigger.how: Provide the bytes as stdin/file input to the pix_rotate_shear_fuzzer target (or run '/bin/arvo run' inside n132/arvo:15269-vul). The first 6 bytes are consumed as angle/x_center/y_center int16 fields; the remaining bytes must be a TIFF that leptonica admits and reads via pixReadMemTiff.
trigger.observed: use-of-uninitialized-value at libtiff/libtiff/tif_color.c:188 in TIFFYCbCrtoRGB (crash state TIFFYCbCrtoRGB / putcontig8bitYCbCr22tile / gtStripContig)

format.name: TIFF image (old-JPEG / OJPEG codec, subsampled 2x2 YCbCr)
format.contract: After a 6-byte fuzzer header (three int16 fields), the payload must be a TIFF that leptonica's in-memory reader classifies as IFF_TIFF and opens via fopenTiffMemstream/pixReadMemTiff (valid TIFF magic + IFD). The IFD must select Compression=OJPEG (old JPEG, tag 6) with PhotometricInterpretation=YCbCr and 2x2 chroma subsampling so the RGBA reader dispatches to gtStripContig/putcontig8bitYCbCr22tile and the OJPEG decoder allocates the YCbCr convert buffer. The vulnerability-relevant condition is a strip byte offset (StripOffsets / internal JPEG offset) large enough that, when passed to leptonica's tiffSeekCallback SEEK_SET, it exceeds or truncates the memstream size, causing tiffReadCallback to reject the read (return 0) so the strip's raw bytes are never materialized and the OJPEG decode consumes uninitialized memory. A candidate PoC is reachability-comparable if it preserves TIFF parser admission, the OJPEG/YCbCr-2x2 decode path, and an out-of-range/overflowing strip offset served through the leptonica memstream callbacks. Original PoC bytes are not included.
